title: Counit-transpose coefficient comparison and tensor coherence
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $r\geq m\geq1$, $A=A_r=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ and $B=A_m=\mathbf Z/\ell^m\mathbf Z$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of finite type and pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between Noetherian schemes (schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and suppose $f$ is compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable]. Work in ordinary etale derived categories of constant-coefficient module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Here bounded constructible means finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, each constructible as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]; finite Tor amplitude means that some interval $[a,b]$ contains the cohomology of the derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf on that same small etale site. Write $P_A=Rf_{!,A}$, $G_A=f_A^\times$, $P_A\dashv G_A$ with counit $\varepsilon_A$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and likewise over $B$; put $\omega_{f,A}=G_AA_Y$ and $S_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$ on $T=X,Y$. Let $b_M:S_YP_AM\xrightarrow{\sim}P_BS_XM$ be the canonical coefficient comparison on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs: form it on a compactification by the identity/zero extension-by-zero tensor comparison and the proper coefficient map adjoint to the proper inverse-image counit tensored with $B$. Suppose the $b$ for consecutive quotient rings obey their tensor-associativity cocycle. For bounded constructible finite-Tor $K$ on $Y$, the object $G_AK$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor, so $b_{G_AK}$ is defined. The counit transpose $c_K:S_XG_AK\to G_BS_YK$, specified by
$$\varepsilon_B(S_YK)\circ P_B(c_K)=S_Y(\varepsilon_A(K))\circ b_{G_AK}^{-1},$$
is natural in $K$. For $r\geq m\geq n\geq1$, one has $c_{r,n,K}=c_{m,n,S_{r,m}K}\circ S_{m,n}(c_{r,m,K})$ under the canonical derived tensor associators. If $\phi_{A,K}:f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}\to G_AK$ is the canonical tensor map, adjoint to inverse compact-support projection followed by $1\otimes\varepsilon_A(A_Y)$ [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], then
$$c_K\circ S_X(\phi_{A,K})=\phi_{B,S_YK}\circ(1\otimes c_{A_Y})$$
under the canonical scalar, pullback and tensor identifications. In any Cartesian base change of $f$ to a Noetherian scheme for which the base-changed morphism is compactifiable, the exceptional base-change maps $\beta$ of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] commute with these $c$: applying scalar extension and $\beta$ in either order gives the same map from $S_{X'}g'^*G_AK$ to $G_{B,f'}g^*S_YK$. These assertions do not assume invertibility of $c$.

proof.text: First check the domains, without treating $A\to B$ as flat. For a bounded constructible ordinary-etale $K$, put $\widetilde K=\nu^*K$. The finite-ring origin equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] makes $\widetilde K$ intrinsically constructible. Since our schemes are Noetherian and hence qcqs and $A$ is Noetherian, [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] transfers the Tor interval $[a,b]$ of $K$ to $\widetilde K$. Apply [lem-pur-finite-reduction-constructibility] with origin $K$: it supplies a flat K-flat representative $Q$ of $K$ supported in $[a,b]$, and says that $S K$ is again bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, with the same interval, in the ordinary-etale category. This also applies to each further quotient and gives its canonical tensor associator. These comparisons are used only to check domains; all maps in the subsequent argument are ordinary-etale maps.

source.place: Domain check for (2); finite reduction on flat models in sk-lem-sp-reduction.proof.md

proof.text: Take $N=\ell^r$. The hypotheses of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] hold, and give $\omega_{f,A}=L[2d]$, with $L$ etale locally free of rank one, and $G_AK\cong f^*K\otimes_A^L L[2d]$. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] computes $f^*K$ by $f^*Q$. Pullback preserves flat terms and K-flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. Tensoring with $L$ is exact and preserves flat terms: after a trivializing etale restriction it is tensoring with $A$, hence the identity; exactness and flatness are checked on the localized sheaf categories. Thus $f^*Q\otimes_A L[2d]$ is a bounded flat model in $[a-2d,b-2d]$. The flat-model criterion [lem-kun-flat-bounded-tor-amplitude] gives that same Tor interval for $G_AK$. No orientation of $L$ is used.

source.place: Statement and final paragraph; bounded-flat-model consequence

proof.text: The cohomology of $f^*K$ is $f^*\mathcal H^i(K)$ by exactness [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-set-pullback]. Refine a trivializing etale covering of $L$ to a finite affine covering using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings]; their disjoint union $u:V\to X$ is qcqs and surjective. On $V$, $u^*G_AK\cong u^*f^*K[2d]$ by [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], so each cohomology sheaf is constructible there. Descent of constructibility [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-surjective-pullback] gives constructibility on $X$. Together with the preceding step this proves the asserted bounded constructible finite-Tor domain of $G_AK$, hence of $b_{G_AK}$. The same argument applies over $B$ and after the stated Noetherian base change.

source.place: Locally free rank-one conclusion; constructibility consequence

proof.text: Use the adjunction $P_B\dashv G_B$ of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The mate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], with left square $b^{-1}:P_BS_X\to S_YP_A$, defines a natural transformation $c:S_XG_A\to G_BS_Y$ on the domain checked above. Explicitly $c_K=G_B(S_Y\varepsilon_A(K)\circ b_{G_AK}^{-1})\circ\eta_B(S_XG_AK)$; its transpose is exactly the displayed identity in the statement. For $h:K\to K'$, transposing both $G_B(S_Yh)c_K$ and $c_{K'}S_X(G_Ah)$ gives $S_Y(h\varepsilon_A(K))b_{G_AK}^{-1}$, by naturality of $\varepsilon_A$ and $b$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves naturality. This constructs a morphism and does not infer that a mate of an isomorphism is invertible.

source.place: (2), definition of the counit transpose and its naturality

proof.text:
For $A\to B\to C$ write $S^{AB},S^{BC},S^{AC}$ for scalar extension, identifying successive tensors by their canonical associators from step 1. Transpose $c^{BC}_{S^{AB}K}\circ S^{BC}c^{AB}_K$ under $P_C\dashv G_C$. The defining counit identity for $c^{BC}$ gives
$$S^{BC}\varepsilon_B(S^{AB}K)\circ(b^{BC}_{G_BS^{AB}K})^{-1}\circ P_C S^{BC}c^{AB}_K.$$
Naturality of $b^{BC}$ changes this to
$$S^{BC}(\varepsilon_B(S^{AB}K)\circ P_Bc^{AB}_K)\circ(b^{BC}_{S^{AB}G_AK})^{-1}.$$
Substitute the defining identity for $c^{AB}$; the result is
$$S^{AC}\varepsilon_A(K)\circ S^{BC}(b^{AB}_{G_AK})^{-1}\circ(b^{BC}_{S^{AB}G_AK})^{-1}=S^{AC}\varepsilon_A(K)\circ(b^{AC}_{G_AK})^{-1}.$$
The equality is the assumed cocycle for $b$. This is the transpose of $c^{AC}_K$, proving the quotient cocycle by adjunction. Equivalently it is precisely vertical mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1), applied to the inverses of the $b$ squares.

source.place: (2), quotient cocycle, written with its naturality substitution

proof.text:
Write $\pi_A(K,M):K\otimes_A^LP_AM\to P_A(f^*K\otimes_A^LM)$ for compact-support projection (using symmetry to put $K$ first). On the compactification $f=pj$, its proper constituent is the counit-defined projection isomorphism [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and its open constituent is [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to $p$ with horizontal ringed-topos maps $(T_{\mathrm{et}},B_T)\to(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_T)$ given by the identity underlying topos and $A_T\to B_T$. Their derived pullbacks are $S_T$; their proper exchange is exactly the coefficient map in the question, since both are transposes of the scalar-extended proper counit. The cited projection/exchange identity therefore gives compatibility for the proper constituent. For the open constituent the two maps are the same balancing map $(k\otimes m)\otimes b\mapsto(k\otimes1)\otimes(m\otimes b)$ on the open and zero off it; its K-flat derivation is the cited open tensor identity. Composing gives
$$b_{f^*K\otimes M}\circ S_Y\pi_A(K,M)=\pi_B(S_YK,S_XM)\circ(1\otimes b_M),$$
under the pullback/tensor identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Only instances where the displayed $b$ are defined are needed, in particular $M=\omega_{f,A}$.

proof.text:
Put $H=f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_{f,A}$. By [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], the transpose of $\phi_{A,K}$ is
$$(1\otimes\varepsilon_A(A_Y))\circ\pi_A(K,\omega_{f,A})^{-1}.$$
Transpose $c_K\circ S_X\phi_{A,K}$ under $P_B\dashv G_B$. Naturality of $b$ and the definition of $c$ give
$$S_Y\big((1\otimes\varepsilon_A(A_Y))\circ\pi_A^{-1}\big)\circ b_H^{-1}.$$
For the other side, naturality of $\pi_B$ in its second argument gives transpose
$$(1\otimes[\varepsilon_B(B_Y)\circ P_Bc_{A_Y}])\circ\pi_B(S_YK,S_X\omega_{f,A})^{-1}.$$
Replace the bracket by $S_Y\varepsilon_A(A_Y)\circ b_{\omega_{f,A}}^{-1}$. The projection identity of step 6, inverted and followed by this counit, makes these two displayed maps identical. The adjunction bijection proves the required tensor-map equality. Unit constraints identify $S_YA_Y=B_Y$; the scalar tensor and pullback comparisons are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

source.place: (3), tensor map paragraph, with both transposes expanded

proof.text:
For base change choose the same compactification $f=pj$ over both rings and its pullback over $Y'$. Let $h:\overline X'\to\overline X$. Write $q:S_YRp_{*,A}\to Rp_{*,B}S_{\overline X}$ for the proper coefficient map, $q'$ for its pullback analogue, and $e_R:g^*Rp_{*,R}\to Rp'_{*,R}h^*$ for proper exchange. Then
$$e_B(SL)\circ g^*q_L=q'_{h^*L}\circ S(e_A(L)),$$
where $Sg^*=g^*S$ and $Sh^*=h^*S$ are the canonical identifications. Indeed, transpose either side under $p_B'^*\dashv Rp'_{*,B}$. By mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1), its transpose is the single map
$$p_B'^*Sg^*Rp_{*,A}L\cong Sh^*p_A^*Rp_{*,A}L\xrightarrow{Sh^*\varepsilon_{p,A,L}}Sh^*L.$$
The pullback identification is the same on both paths: on flat K-flat models the coefficient balancing map is $s\otimes a\mapsto sa$, and its compatibility with inverse image follows from the canonical tensor/pullback construction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus no invertibility assertion about an exceptional mate enters this comparison.

proof.text:
Let $E_R:g^*P_R\xrightarrow{\sim}P'_Rg'^*$ denote compact-support base change, with exactly the proper/open normalization of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Its open part and the open part of $b$ commute with each other: over the pulled-back open both orders are the identity followed by scalar balancing, and off that open both are zero. This is an equality of the underived sheaf comparisons before passing to K-flat complexes, using the extension-by-zero stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and then its derived tensor identification [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. Combine that open equality with step 8 for the proper part, and apply naturality when moving the proper map past the open map. Their ordered composites are
$$E_{B,S_XM}\circ g^*b_M=b'_{g'^*M}\circ S_{Y'}E_{A,M}.$$
These are maps $S_{Y'}g^*P_AM\to P'_BS_{X'}g'^*M$. The cited compact-support comparison theorem makes the calculation on the pulled-back compactification the calculation for the specified compactification-independent $E_R$. Only bounded constructible finite-Tor $M$ and its pullbacks are used here.

proof.text:
Finally [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] defines $\beta_{R,K}$ by transposing $g^*\varepsilon_R(K)\circ E_{R,G_RK}^{-1}$ under $P'_R\dashv G'_R$. Transpose the two maps in the question under $P'_B\dashv G'_B$, identifying scalar extension and geometric pullback as above. For $\beta_{B,S_YK}\circ g'^*c_K$, naturality of $E_B$ and the counit identity for $c_K$ give
$$g^*S_Y\varepsilon_A(K)\circ g^*b_{G_AK}^{-1}\circ E_{B,S_XG_AK}^{-1}.$$
For $c'_{g^*K}\circ S_{X'}\beta_{A,K}$, naturality of $b'$ and the counit identities for $c'$ and $\beta_A$ give
$$S_{Y'}g^*\varepsilon_A(K)\circ S_{Y'}E_{A,G_AK}^{-1}\circ(b'_{g'^*G_AK})^{-1}.$$
Step 9, inverted, identifies the two right-hand pairs of factors. The first factors agree under $g^*S_Y=S_{Y'}g^*$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] proves the base-change equality, with target $G'_Bg^*S_YK$. The hypotheses on $f'$ and $Y'$ are exactly those required for the cited smooth base-change theorem and for the domain checks in steps 1–3. This finishes all clauses without assuming $c$ invertible.

proof.text: For the auxiliary theorem compactSupportMap_isIso, the proper morphism c.g has Noetherian source: finite type preserves local Noetherianity and quasi-compactness over the compact target gives compactness. Apply lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension to the finite quotient map and the open extension of M. Its first clause proves that the scalarMate component in compactSupportMap is invertible. The other factor is proper direct image of the isomorphism openIso. Their composite is invertible. This avoids a separate bounded-flat-model or totalization argument for this auxiliary theorem; the domain calculations in the main theorem remain open.

For tensorIso_existsUnique use the already proved etaleHomTensorComparison_existsUnique, whose binary comparison is natural and normalized on flat-term K-flat pairs. Package its inverses as a natural isomorphism on the product category. The scalar cochain representatives are a natural transformation: apply the scalar derived adjunction to the ordinary cochain unit followed by the exact-restriction localization comparison. For arbitrary cochain P,Q choose flat-term K-flat resolutions Pprime -> P and Qprime -> Q. The two sides of TensorNormalizationAux are components of natural transformations of cochain pairs. The source maps of these resolutions are invertible after localization and derived tensor. Cancel their composite and use the known normalization at Pprime,Qprime. Uniqueness follows by restricting any all-complex-normalized comparison to the flat-term K-flat pairs and invoking the existing binary uniqueness theorem.

For siteTensorIso_existsUnique the new generic SiteTensorNormalizationAux is exactly TensorNormalizationAux on small-etale sheaves, with derivedTensor constants in its argument type. TensorNormalization specializes this generic predicate. Thus the normalized chosen isomorphism has literally the site tensor type: use reflexive heterogeneous equality for existence and eq_of_heq for uniqueness. This representation avoids repeated comparison of nested sheafification proofs; the all-complex normalization equation and the canonical comparison are unchanged.

For unitIso_existsUnique the unit complex is K-flat, so the scalar cochain representative is invertible by the exact-right-adjoint K-flat representative theorem. Ordinary scalar extension preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms because, after faithful exact restriction, it is tensoring with the constant coefficient sheaf; tensoring an acyclic K-flat complex is acyclic. The localization unit comparison is invertible, as is ordinary scalar extension of the unit. Compose these three isomorphisms and the inverse target localization unit comparison. Its hom satisfies UnitNormalizationAux by cancellation, and cancellation also proves uniqueness.

proof_origin.place: B3 proves the tensor, site tensor transport and unit normalization auxiliary theorems by the recorded arguments. The main exceptional_coefficient_comparison theorem and its ten-step plan remain unchanged, as does the previously proved compactSupportMap_isIso.
